memoryTip: Dental amalgam mixes metals — amalgamate = blend into one.
correctPassage: The two small clinics will amalgamate next year into a single regional center.
wrongPassages: Managers hoped to amalgamate the budget deficit by spending even more on marketing.
She tried to amalgamate the argument by refusing to hear any opposing evidence.
The storm will amalgamate overnight as the cold front weakens and skies clear.

definition: formally announce or make widely known
memoryTip: Pro-mulgate: put the rule out so everyone hears it.
correctPassage: The agency will promulgate the new safety standards before the compliance deadline.
wrongPassages: They hoped to promulgate the surplus by quietly burying it in a locked warehouse.
The cleaner will promulgate the spill by pushing it under the nearest mat.
She tried to promulgate the rumor by refusing to speak about it to anyone.

memoryTip: Reciprocal: you give, I give back — mutual benefit.
correctPassage: Trade negotiators insisted on reciprocity so each country would open its markets equally.
wrongPassages: Under a policy of reciprocity, only one side ever paid while the other kept taking.
She practiced reciprocity by accepting every favor and never returning any.
The treaty’s reciprocity clause required gifts to flow in one direction only.

memoryTip: En-tail: the decision drags consequences along behind it.
correctPassage: Accepting the fellowship will entail relocating for at least two years.
wrongPassages: Accepting the grant will entail nothing: no reports, no work, and no consequences at all.
The software will entail your password into one emoji.
Please entail the chairs into neat rows after lunch.

definition: demand or specify as a condition of an agreement
memoryTip: Stipulate the terms — spell out conditions in the deal.
correctPassage: The contract stipulates that all research data remain public for five years.
wrongPassages: He tried to stipulate the error by deleting the logs so no one could check.
She hoped to stipulate the fever by ignoring the symptoms until morning.
The runner will stipulate failure by swallowing exceptions and reporting success.
